hello.note: Time-of-day greetings like selamat pagi are just as common. Many Muslims greet with assalamualaikum.

goodbye.note: Casual: dah! Selamat jalan is said to someone setting off on a trip.

please.note: Tolong asks for help or a favour. When offering (please, go ahead / help yourself), say silakan.

thank_you.note: Very grateful: terima kasih banyak. Casual: makasih.

yes.note: Iya is softer and very common in speech.

no.note: Casual: nggak. Bukan negates nouns instead: bukan yang ini (not this one).

sorry.note: Fuller apology: saya minta maaf. Formal: mohon maaf.

excuse_me.note: Also said when passing in front of someone. Adding Pak (to a man) or Bu (to a woman) is even politer.

good_morning.note: Until about 11 a.m. Then selamat siang (midday) and selamat sore (afternoon).

how_are_you.note: Warmer with a title: apa kabar, Pak? (to a man) / apa kabar, Bu? (to a woman).

im_fine.note: Also: kabar baik. To ask back: bagaimana dengan Anda?

whats_your_name.note: Anda is polite but formal; people often say Bapak (sir) or Ibu (madam) instead. Casual: namanya siapa?

my_name_is.note: Saya is the polite 'I'; with friends, aku.

nice_to_meet_you.note: Casual: salam kenal. Also: senang bertemu dengan Anda.

where_from.note: In speech also: asalnya dari mana?

speak_english.note: In speech often just: bisa bahasa Inggris?

dont_understand.note: Also: saya tidak paham. Casual: nggak ngerti.

speak_slowly.note: Softer, as a question: bisa bicara lebih pelan?

where.note: Where to: ke mana? Where from: dari mana?

what.note: To ask someone to repeat, maaf? or bagaimana? is politer than a bare apa?

when.note: Only for questions; in statements 'when' is ketika or waktu.

how_much.note: Pointing at something, simply: ini berapa?

where_bathroom.note: Also: kamar kecil (more polite) or WC, said weh-seh.

can_you_help.note: Also very natural: boleh minta tolong? (may I ask a favour?)

what_time.note: Also: sekarang jam berapa? Formal: pukul berapa sekarang?

what_means.note: About a word: apa arti kata ini?

one.note: In compounds it becomes se-: sepuluh (10), seratus (100), seribu (1,000).

four.note: The e is a short 'uh' sound, as in about. Same in enam, delapan and sembilan.

seven.note: The final h is lightly breathed, not silent.

ten.note: Literally 'one ten'. 11 is sebelas, 20 is dua puluh.

water.note: Plain drinking water (literally 'white water'). Air, said a-ir, alone is water in general.

tea.note: Usually served sweet; for unsweetened ask for teh tawar. Iced tea: es teh.

menu_please.note: To call staff: Mas! (to a young man) or Mbak! (to a young woman).

bill_please.note: Also common: minta bill-nya, or just ask the total: totalnya berapa?

no_meat.note: Daging often means red meat only; to be clear add: ayam dan ikan juga tidak (no chicken or fish either).

left.note: Calling kiri! is also how you ask a minibus (angkot) driver to stop.

stop_here.note: To a woman driver, end with Bu. Very common too: di sini saja, Pak (right here is fine).

hotel.note: Same word as in English. Cheaper guesthouses: penginapan or losmen.

train_station.note: Stasiun alone usually means the train station; a bus station is a terminal.

want_to_go.note: More formal: saya ingin pergi ke …

is_it_far.note: Casual: jauh nggak? More formal: apakah jauh dari sini?

one_ticket.note: Ending with ya softens a request, like please. Fuller: saya mau beli satu tiket.

too_expensive.note: Casual: mahal banget! To bargain: bisa kurang? (can you go lower?)

id_like_this.note: Also: saya ambil yang ini (I'll take this one).

just_looking.note: Also: lihat-lihat dulu, ya (just looking for now).

pay_card.note: More formal: bisa bayar dengan kartu? Credit card: kartu kredit; debit card: kartu debit.

cash.note: Also: uang tunai. In speech many simply say cash.

later.note: Vague on purpose: it can mean in a minute or in a few days.

good_evening.note: From about 6 p.m. Late afternoon: selamat sore.

good_night.note: Only before sleep. When leaving at night, people say selamat malam, the same as good evening.

see_you_later.note: Also: sampai ketemu lagi (see you again).

wait_moment.note: Very common: sebentar, ya! Formal: mohon tunggu sebentar.

help.note: The same tolong that makes a request polite.

dont_feel_well.note: Also: saya tidak enak badan. Saya sakit means I'm ill.

pharmacy.note: Small shops with basic medicines: toko obat.

hospital.note: Often shortened to RS on signs.

lost_phone.note: HP (said ha-peh) is the everyday word for a mobile phone; formal: ponsel.

be_careful.note: Also a friendly goodbye to someone setting off: hati-hati di jalan.

no_problem.note: Casual: nggak apa-apa (often said gapapa). Also: tidak masalah.

dont_know.note: Casual: nggak tahu, often said nggak tau.

i_like_it.note: Pointing at something: saya suka yang ini.

im_happy.note: Bahagia is a deeper, lasting happiness: saya bahagia.

welcome.note: Inviting a guest in: silakan masuk.

congratulations.note: The same selamat that starts greetings like selamat pagi.
